evidence.text: The entry analyzes 蛋 as 虫 with abbreviated phonetic 延 and gives animal egg as its basic sense. It says 蛋 is very late and absent from oracle bone, bronze, Shuowen, and Guangyun; cites 字彙補 for “蛋, anciently written 蜑” and “俗呼鳥卵為蛋”; and gives egg examples from Journey to the West, chapter 32, and Dream of the Red Chamber, chapter 40. It lists egg-shaped-object and abusive uses without dating those extensions. These are the entry’s assertions, not independently established chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 蛋

evidence.field: 延 historical forms and role in 蛋
evidence.text: The entry says oracle-bone and early bronze 延 forms show a person walking on a road, analyzed as 彳 plus 止, with an early sense of traveling afar. It reports that forms with 丿 appear in late Warring States Qin slips and quotes Shuowen’s analysis 从㢟、丿聲. This supports 延’s separate graphic history; it does not establish an object name or a whole-graph loan in 蛋.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 延

evidence.text: The entry gives Zhengzhang-style Old Chinese 延 *lan and *lans and places 蛋 in 延’s phonetic series with reconstruction *l'aːns. This is secondary database evidence for a sound-series relationship; it does not establish the origin of the spoken egg word.
evidence.title: 蛋 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: The 蛋 entry displays Mandarin dàn. The 延 entry displays Mandarin yán and Guangyun fanqie 以然 for its level-tone reading, with a separate departing-tone reading 予線. Thus the modern Mandarin readings differ. In the Zhengzhang reconstruction cited by the phonetic-series entry, 延 *lan/*lans and 蛋 *l'aːns are similar within that system. This is compatible with a phonetic role, not proof of lexical borrowing.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 蛋; 延 entries

evidence.source: 臺灣教育部《異體字字典》
evidence.text: The entry states that 蛋 is not recorded in Shuowen. It gives an egg sense with examples attributed to Guan Hanqing’s Yuan drama and Rulin Waishi; a shape-like sense with late-imperial literary examples; abusive uses with Ming-Qing and later novel examples; and the southern coastal people sense, including a Song History quotation. These examples document uses but do not by themselves prove a sequence of semantic derivation.
evidence.kind: government dictionary with cited textual examples
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》— 蛋 A03630

evidence.source: 胡雲鳳, “說「蛋」,” 國立臺灣師範大學期刊資料庫
evidence.text: The abstract argues that Tang俗字 evidence shows 蛋 arose as a graphic corruption/change of 蜑 around the Tang period. It separately dates the poultry-egg sense to about Northern Song, developing through Yuan and Ming and becoming established by Qing. This is the author’s conclusion as reported in an accessible abstract; the underlying examples were not independently collated here.
evidence.title: 期刊論文 — 胡雲鳳〈說「蛋」〉

evidence.field: Middle Chinese reading associated with 蜑
evidence.text: The Guangyun small-rhyme entry 但 gives fanqie 徒旱, 定 initial, 上聲, 寒 rhyme, open first division, and includes 蜑 among its characters. This is a Middle Chinese comparison for 蜑; it does not give 蛋 its own Guangyun reading, consistent with the cited claim that 蛋 is absent from Guangyun.
evidence.title: 但 — 小韻 — 廣韻 — 韻典網

evidence.field: 延 bronze image description and reuse rights
evidence.text: The file description identifies 延-bronze.svg as a modern vector depiction of 延 in Western Zhou bronze-script style, sourced through character-reference databases including the CUHK database and Hanziyuan. Its description states the image is reused by courtesy under Richard Sears website copyright terms; reuse should follow the linked agreement rather than assume public-domain status.
evidence.title: File:延-bronze.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: 卵 seal image description and reuse rights
evidence.text: The file description identifies 卵-seal.svg as a modern vector depiction in Shuowen seal-script style, with an attribution to the Hanziyuan data image S10122. The page describes the SVG representation as public domain, with attribution appreciated. It illustrates the older graph used for egg, not 蛋’s form or its formation.
evidence.title: File:卵-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: search snippet for 延 phonetic series membership
evidence.text: A search result lists 蛋 and 蜑 among characters in the 延 phonetic series and displays Zhengzhang-style variants in the series. The individual database page was not inspected during this invocation; this is treated only as corroborating search-result evidence.
evidence.title: 聲符表 — 上古音系 — 韻典網

gaps: No directly verified historical glyph image for 蛋 or 蜑 was found. The延 bronze SVG description page reports identity and reuse terms, but the page failed when opened and direct file URLs were inaccessible; it is not proposed as a downloadable candidate.
The Commons 卵 seal image is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph, and depicts 卵 rather than 蛋; it is contextual only and is not proposed as a glyph candidate.

The detailed Tang graphic evidence underlying the proposed 蜑-to-蛋 corruption was not directly collated; only a scholarly abstract was inspected. The relation asserted there is chronological, but precise witnesses and variant shapes remain unchecked.

The source-word origin for the spoken egg word remains unsettled. A proposal relating 蛋 to 彈 (‘pellet’) appears in secondary material, but separate earliest attestations and a borrowing mechanism were not verified. A reconstruction of 蛋 does not establish the name or pronunciation of any depicted object; no such object-based borrowing is established here.
The semantic contribution of 虫 is a conventional component analysis. Evidence inspected does not establish a specific original referent such as snake eggs.

Earliest attested egg use remains uncertain: a scholarly abstract argues Northern Song onset, while CUHK cites a Southern Song-attributed text and later works. No independent chronology was reconstructed from those examples.
Dates and semantic links for egg-shaped senses and abusive uses are not demonstrated by the inspected dated examples; gloss order alone cannot establish chronology.
No Japanese-origin claim is supported. Japanese readings are conventional readings and do not establish Japanese formation.
No historical image was visually inspected; all image descriptions and reuse information are recorded as source descriptions only.

limitations.text: Fresh searches found no usable directly identified 蛋 or 蜑 image with confirmed direct image URL and reusable provenance. 延-bronze.svg is a related phonetic component candidate with a Commons page describing it as a modern vector based on Hanziyuan and reuse by permission, but the page and direct file links failed in the web tool, so its image URL and permission details could not be verified sufficiently for proposal. No artifact photograph is claimed.
A Commons seal-script vector for 卵 was found with public-domain reuse description, but it depicts a distinct older egg graph and cannot stand in for 蛋’s graphic history.
